MeasureTheory.combine_estimates₁.statement:
Let $\alpha$ and $\alpha'$ be types equipped with measurable-space structures $m$ and $m'$, let $\mu$ be a measure on $\alpha$ and $
u$ a measure on $\alpha'$. Let $E_1$ be a topological space carrying an extended-seminormed additive monoid structure ($\mathrm{ESeminormedAddMonoid}$), and let $E_2$ be a topological space with a continuous extended norm $\|\cdot\|_e$ ($\mathrm{ContinuousENorm}$). Let $T$ be an operator sending functions $\alpha 	o E_1$ to functions $\alpha' 	o E_2$. Let $p, q, p_0, q_0, p_1, q_1, t$ be elements of the extended nonnegative reals $[0,\infty]$, and let $A, C_0, C_1$ be nonnegative real numbers. Assume $A > 0$, $C_0 > 0$, $C_1 > 0$, $p_0 \in (0, q_0]$, $p_1 \in (0, q_1]$, $t \in (0,1)$, $p_0 < p_1$, $q_0 
e q_1$, $p^{-1} = (1-t)p_0^{-1} + t\,p_1^{-1}$ and $q^{-1} = (1-t)q_0^{-1} + t\,q_1^{-1}$ (arithmetic in $[0,\infty]$, with truncated subtraction). Let $f : \alpha 	o E_1$ satisfy $f \in L^p(\mu)$ ($\mathrm{MemLp}\ f\ p\ \mu$) and $0 < \|f\|_{L^p(\mu)} < \infty$, where $\|\cdot\|_{L^p(\mu)}$ is $\mathrm{eLpNorm}$. Assume $\mathrm{SubadditiveTrunc}\ T\ A\ f\ 
u$, i.e. for every $a \in (0,\infty]$, for $
u$-almost every $y \in \alpha'$, $\|T(\mathrm{trunc}\,f\,a + \mathrm{truncCompl}\,f\,a)(y)\|_e \le A\,(\|T(\mathrm{trunc}\,f\,a)(y)\|_e + \|T(\mathrm{truncCompl}\,f\,a)(y)\|_e)$. Assume $\mathrm{HasWeakType}\ T\ p_1\ q_1\ \mu\ 
u\ C_1$ and $\mathrm{HasWeakType}\ T\ p_0\ q_0\ \mu\ 
u\ C_0$, i.e. for $i \in \{0,1\}$ and every $g \in L^{p_i}(\mu)$, $T g$ is $
u$-a.e. strongly measurable and its weak $L^{q_i}(
u)$ norm ($\mathrm{wnorm}$) is at most $C_i \|g\|_{L^{p_i}(\mu)}$. Assume $\mathrm{PreservesAEStrongMeasurability}\ T\ p$ (with respect to $\mu$ and $
u$), i.e. $T g$ is $
u$-a.e. strongly measurable for every $g \in L^p(\mu)$. Finally let $\mathrm{spf}$ be a $\mathrm{ScaledPowerFunction}$ equal to $\mathrm{ChoiceScale.spf\_ch}$ applied to the above hypotheses (the particular choice of scaled power function used in the proof of the real interpolation theorem, with exponent $\sigma = \zeta(p_0,q_0,p_1,q_1,t)$ where $\zeta = \mathrm{ComputationsChoiceExponent.\zeta}$ and $t$ is taken as a real number). Below, for $x \in [0,\infty]$, $ ar x$ denotes the real number $\mathrm{toReal}(x)$ (equal to $x$ if $x<\infty$ and to $0$ if $x=\infty$); $\mathbf{1}[P]$ is $1$ if $P$ holds and $0$ otherwise; $| ar q -  ar q_i|^{-1}$ is computed in $\mathbb{R}$ (with the convention $0^{-1} = 0$) and then mapped to $[0,\infty]$ by $\mathrm{ENNReal.ofReal}$; and all powers are powers of elements of $[0,\infty]$ with real exponents. Then
$$\|T f\|_{L^q(
u)} \le \mathrm{ofReal}(2A)\cdot q^{\overline{q^{-1}}}\cdot\Big(\mathbf{1}[q_1 < \infty]\,\mathrm{ofReal} ig(| ar q -  ar q_1|^{-1} ig) + \mathbf{1}[q_0 < \infty]\,\mathrm{ofReal} ig(| ar q -  ar q_0|^{-1} ig)\Big)^{\overline{q^{-1}}}\cdot C_0^{\overline{1-t}}\cdot C_1^{ ar t}\cdot\|f\|_{L^p(\mu)}.$$
